consts:
core/store/cache.py - layout fingerprint -> PoRecipe cache.

The fingerprint is derived from a NORMALIZED skeleton (volatile numbers / style /
color / model codes masked to "#") plus coarse structural markers, so two POs of
the same layout (e.g. LPP 637JO and LPP XL901) collide to ONE recipe, while
different layouts (LPP vs COLIN'S vs SAKHA) stay distinct.

Cache dir: %APPDATA%\Purchase Order Extractor V2\recipe_cache\

Collapse immediately-repeated token windows so the fingerprint ignores
    ORDER VOLUME (item-row count, size-column count, per-size totals) but keeps
    TEMPLATE identity (the set/order of label words).

    The raw fingerprint text is page-concatenated tokens (one line per page), so
    the variable volume shows up as a *repeated subsequence* -- e.g. a matrix grid
    'S M L # S M L # S M L #' or line-item rows '# # BLUE # # # # # RED # # #'.
    A plain '#'-run collapse cannot catch that; we need subsequence RLE.

Collapse any maximal run of pure-'#' value tokens to ONE '#'.

    After digit/word/code masking, header regions (vendor address, free-text
    notes, parenthesized clauses) become sequences like '# ## ### #' whose LENGTH
    varies per PO even though every token is a masked value. Collapsing pure-#
    runs makes the fingerprint insensitive to how many content words a header
    block carries, while structural punctuation ('(', ')', '<', '>', '+', '!',
    '=') is preserved so row/column layout still discriminates templates.

Collapse parenthesized CONTENT groups to a single '(#)' and merge runs.

    Raw parenthesized spans -- (MM), (invoice), (a) (b) (c) (d) size legends,
    penalty clauses, country codes -- are all variable CONTENT, not layout.
    Their count/order must not vary the fingerprint; a line-item ROW that sits
    inside parentheses also reduces to '(#)', which is fine because the
    <<HAS_...>> markers still separate line_items from matrix layouts.

Mask volatile tokens so the fingerprint reflects LAYOUT, not data.

    The fingerprint is content-INsensitive: same customer template (same column
    structure / header labels) collides to ONE recipe regardless of product
    words (MEN'S vs LADIES'), style-code formats (ABC-DEF vs ABC-DEF-GHI),
    size legends (a) b) c) d)), vendor-address wording, or parenthesized header
    clauses -- while genuinely different templates stay distinct via the
    <<HAS_...>> structural markers plus the ORDERED set of distinct body token
    TYPES (count-insensitive, so header word-/clause-count no longer varies fp).

    Pipeline: per-token masking -> RLE -> value-run collapse -> paren normalize
    -> distinct-token-type sequence.

On a fingerprint-scheme change, drop orphaned recipe files once.

        Old fingerprints (which encoded row/size counts) never match the new
        volume-insensitive fingerprints, so stale entries would just sit unused.
        Flushing them makes a customer's first post-upgrade PO re-infer cleanly.

Delete a cached recipe (e.g. after it produced 0 order lines).

        Returns True if a file was actually removed. Failures are swallowed by the
        caller, so this never breaks the extraction pipeline.

Delete every cached recipe so all layouts re-infer from scratch.

        Returns the number of recipe files removed. The ``.schema`` marker is
        preserved so the fingerprint scheme is not re-flung. Used by the
        "清除布局指纹" button when a user wants to discard every learned recipe.

Return how many layout recipes are currently cached.

        Counts ``*.json`` files (the ``.schema`` marker is dotfile and ignored).
        Used by the "清除布局指纹 (n)" button to show a live fingerprint count,
        mirroring 1.6.4's "清除客户记忆 (n)".

Return sorted ``<fp>.json`` filenames currently cached.

        Used by the fingerprint manager panel to enumerate every saved layout
        recipe without loading them all. The ``.schema`` marker is a dotfile and
        is ignored.
